title: policy.json: rights
description: Decision rights as data (design parts 4.2, 4.4 and 4.5). Changing any of it is a rule change: the owner's decision.

agent_spend_max_tokens.description: Tokens an agent may commit beyond an approved appetite before the question becomes the owner's (the budget rule).

rules.description: Per rule basis: the default decider, and the conditions under which the owner decides instead of an area owner.

one-way-door.description: Undoing it later is expensive or impossible.

blast-radius.description: It changes more than one area, behaviour users rely on, or the build and release pipeline.

public-commitment.description: It creates or changes something outsiders will depend on: API, naming, file formats, licensing, security posture.

novelty.description: No precedent matches, and the principles do not settle it.

conflicting-evidence.description: Studies, measurements or credible sources disagree, and the choice depends on which is right.

relationship.description: Someone outside will read it as coming from the owner or the project, and it is sensitive.

budget.description: It commits more than agent_spend_max_tokens tokens beyond an approved appetite, or bets a new appetite.

security.description: It adds a dependency, widens a privilege, changes a trust boundary, handles a vulnerability report, or touches secrets.

rule-change.description: It changes policy bounds, decision rights, a skill, an invariant, or the executor contract.

areas.description: The area map. An area owner decides a question only if its basis is in the area's may_decide; otherwise, and where an area has no owners, the owner decides.

owner_when.description: cross-area: the question spans more than one area. direction: it touches strategy, principles or non-goals.
